expected_result: Balance increases once. The leave request can spend that balance. The duplicate credit is rejected. Rejected overtime cannot be credited.

element_or_api: Holiday calendar affects leave span and attendance
steps: 1. Add a holiday on a Wednesday. 2. Request leave Tuesday to Thursday. 3. Check the attendance day on the holiday for an employee who did not work.
expected_result: The leave debits two working days, not three, when the policy excludes holidays. The holiday is not an absence. Removing the holiday before approval recalculates the debit; removing it after approval does not silently rewrite history.

steps: 1. Upload a 1-row file, a 100-row file, and a 101-row file on the bulk onboard control. 2. Include one invalid email, one duplicate email inside the file, one email that already exists, and one row whose manager is a later row in the same file. 3. Read the preview before commit.
test_data: maxItems 100 on employees. Status enum READY WARNING ERROR SKIPPED. Duplicate email qa.dup@example.com on rows 2 and 3. dependsOnRow pointing forward.
expected_result: 1 and 100 rows preview. 101 rows are rejected before any write. Invalid and duplicate rows are ERROR or SKIPPED with codes, and ready rows stay READY. Seat math is shown (limit, used, available, required, blocked). A row that will not fit is SEAT_LIMIT, not a surprise 402 on confirm.

steps: 1. Commit a preview that mixes READY and ERROR rows. 2. Double-click commit. 3. Commit again with the same file after success. 4. Commit when the plan has fewer seats than READY rows.
test_data: 15 ready rows with 1 seat available. Second click within the pending state.
expected_result: ERROR rows are not created. READY rows that fit are created once and each invite result is sent or a visible reason. The button stays pending so the second click does not double-create. Seat overflow creates nothing for the blocked rows and does not partially ignore the preview. Repeating the file skips existing emails.

element_or_api: Bulk onboard field bounds | firstName lastName email designation
steps: 1. Preview a row with firstName length 0, length 1, length 100, and length 101. 2. Email length 254 and 255. 3. Gender value 'UNKNOWN'. 4. topLevelRole true with a 501-character reason.
test_data: Schema: firstName 1-100, email 1-254, gender MALE|FEMALE|OTHER, topLevelRoleReason max 500, employees max 100.
expected_result: Exact maxima preview as READY or WARNING. One over the max is a row error or a 400 for the whole request, and no employee is created. Unknown enum is rejected. The UI shows the row number and does not drop the rest of the file silently.

steps: 1. Resend the invite. 2. Immediately resend again. 3. Copy the invite link. 4. Open the link after expiry and after the user has already joined.
test_data: New hire who has not accepted. Expired token. Already-active user.
expected_result: The first resend returns sent true or a visible reason. The immediate repeat is 429 or a disabled control, not a second live token that invalidates the first without warning. The copied link matches inviteUrl and is not written to a list payload. Expired and consumed links do not sign anyone in.

element_or_api: Bulk reporting update | POST /hr/reporting-lines/bulk-jobs | POST .../commit | GET .../failures.csv
steps: 1. Upload a mapping with one valid row, one unknown employee, one cycle (A reports to B and B reports to A), and one blank manager. 2. Commit only if preview allows. 3. Download failures.csv. 4. Commit the same job twice.
test_data: Statuses PREVIEWED COMMITTING COMMITTED FAILED EXPIRED. Row statuses READY WARNING ERROR SKIPPED COMMITTED FAILED.
expected_result: Preview does not change live managers. Commit applies only committable rows. Cycles and unknown employees are in the failure file and stay on the old manager. A second commit of a COMMITTED job is rejected. An expired preview cannot be committed.

steps: 1. Import a valid CSV, an empty file, a file with a missing email column, and a file whose row count exceeds the endpoint max. 2. Re-import the same file.
test_data: Header row plus one valid candidate and one row with email 'not-an-email'.
expected_result: Valid new candidates appear in /recruitment/candidates/intake. The bad row is reported with a line number and is not created. Re-import does not duplicate the valid candidate. Empty file is a validation error, not a success of zero with a green toast that looks like a completed import.

element_or_api: Bulk shortlist and reject | POST /hr/recruitment/candidates/bulk-shortlist | POST /hr/recruitment/candidates/bulk-reject
steps: 1. Select zero candidates and trigger each bulk action. 2. Select one, then a mix of already-rejected and new candidates. 3. Submit an empty rejection reason if the dialog requires one. 4. Send candidateIds longer than the schema max.
test_data: candidateIds arrays of length 0, 1, and max+1. One id that belongs to another tenant.
expected_result: Zero selection does not call the API. Mixed selection reports shortlisted/skipped or rejected/skipped counts and does not move the skipped rows. Over-max is 400 with no partial writes. A foreign id does not reject that tenant's candidate.

steps: 1. Enroll 1, 100, and 101 candidates in a sequence. 2. Enroll the same candidate twice. 3. Enroll a candidate who has unsubscribed or has no email. 4. Disable the sequence and enroll again.
test_data: candidateIds maxItems 100. Sequence with two steps.
expected_result: 1 and 100 enroll. 101 is rejected with nobody enrolled. Duplicates and undeliverable addresses are skipped and counted. A disabled sequence sends nothing. The inbox or sequence metrics increase only for real enrollments.

element_or_api: Single send is not a bulk mailer | POST /hr/integrations/send-email
steps: 1. Send one valid email from the template or integration surface. 2. Submit to as an array, as a comma-separated list, and with subject length 0, 200, and 201. 3. Burst 20 sequential sends.
test_data: to one address. subject 200 chars. body 10000 chars. Illegal to: ['a@example.com','b@example.com'].
expected_result: One recipient sends. An array or comma-list is 400 because to is a single email. Subject and body bounds are enforced. The burst is rate-limited with 429 rather than silently delivering 20 mails. This endpoint must not be treated as the bulk mailer; bulk mail is sequence enroll.

element_or_api: Client-side bulk reschedule | PATCH /hr/recruitment/interviews/{interviewId} via Promise.all
steps: 1. Select 3 interviews and reschedule from the bulk date control. 2. Make the second PATCH return 409. 3. Select 40 interviews. 4. Leave the date empty and submit.
test_data: Three ids, the middle one already cancelled. Forty ids. Empty bulkNewDate.
expected_result: Empty date does not fire. The 409 leaves the other interviews' results explicit: the UI must not claim all were rescheduled when Promise.all rejects or when some succeeded. Forty parallel PATCHes either stay under the rate limit or back off; a partial success list is shown. There is no server bulk transaction, so a retry must not move the already-updated interviews a second time without the user seeing the new time.

element_or_api: Import job commit and rollback | POST /hr/import/jobs | POST /hr/import/jobs/{jobId}/commit | POST /hr/import/jobs/{jobId}/rollback
steps: 1. Create an import job, commit it, then roll it back. 2. Roll back before commit. 3. Commit twice.
test_data: A small employee or department file accepted by the import job API.
expected_result: Commit applies once. Rollback restores the pre-commit records. Commit-twice and rollback-before-commit are refused. The job page shows the terminal status.

element_or_api: Document rollout email | sendEmail on rollout dialog
steps: 1. Roll out a template to 1 employee and to a selection, with sendEmail on and off. 2. Include an employee with no work email.
test_data: Template offer letter. sendEmail true and false.
expected_result: sendEmail false generates documents and sends no mail. sendEmail true sends one mail per generated document and the toast count matches the API count. The employee without an email is reported and does not fail the whole batch silently.

steps: 1. Send the attendance report to yourself. 2. Submit an empty recipient if the form allows editing it. 3. Send twice quickly.
test_data: Current month. Authorized HR user email.
expected_result: One report is delivered or queued. Empty recipient is a field error. The double send is throttled or produces two intentional sends with two toasts, not a stuck spinner.

steps: 1. Load /hr/settings/workflows. 2. Capture the list response shape. 3. Page forward with the cursor.
test_data: Cursor page { data, pagination: { limit, hasMore, nextCursor } }. An offset stub { page, limit } without pagination is the known break.
expected_result: The page renders. The client asks with cursor/limit, not page. settings and stepCount are read from each row. A response that is only an offset page is a contract failure, not an empty list.

steps: 1. Open the employee profile as HR with hr:sensitive:view and as HR without it. 2. Compare the JSON of the profile read. 3. Search the page for PAN, bank account, and medical notes.
test_data: Fixture employee with PAN, bank account, and a medical note.
expected_result: Without hr:sensitive:view those values are absent from the DOM and the JSON, not merely CSS-hidden. With the permission they render to the holder only. Copy-link and export actions on the page follow the same rule.
